seasonRounds.track_name: Detroit Grand Prix at Belle Isle

penalties.description: The 654 slams into various runoffs intentionally at least four times in a row during practice. The final time, the 654 slams into the barrier in the turn 4 runoff, flying backwards back out and slamming into the 27. The stewards note that this is practice and we are generally not trying to be the fun police. However, flying back onto the track (accidental or not) and negatively affecting others’ practice isn’t fun.

The 73 is ahead of the 13 on exit of turn 2, but the 13 has a slightly better exit. On approach to the full-throttle turn 3 curve, the 73 positions their car a little over a car’s width from the inside wall. The 13 inches into this space, getting enough overlap with the 73 to trigger a spotter call, but not ‘significant’ overlap by definition. 

As the two cars turn-in, the 13 is pinned against the inside wall as the 73 slightly closes the gap between themselves and the inside wall until the two cars collide. Both go fully sideways, but the 73 saves it and continues. The 13 slides across the track, triggering a smaller wreck before stopping against the left wall. The 661 then enters at the end, arguably a bit too quickly with yellow flags waving, and slams into the 13. Both receive terminal damage.

The stewards have elected to treat this for the most part as though it were an incident that took place on a straight, similar to how we have penalized crashes at sections like Mid-Ohio’s turn 3, Road Atlanta’s turn 9 or Mosport’s turn 7.

The 80 enters turn 2 on the outside of the 23. The 23 goes slightly deep and clears the 80 but impacts the wall on exit, slowing slightly. The 77 uses the slow lines taken by the battling cars ahead took to jump to the inside of the 80 mid-corner as the 23 clears them, getting up to the door of the 80 by corner exit. At the exit of the corner, the 80 tries to pull to the right of the 23 due to their large speed difference after the 23’s wall strike, unaware of the 77’s new presence. The two collide and the 77 impacts the inside wall, towing due to the damage.

On approach to turn 4, the 27 and 29 are side-by-side. As they turn-in, the 27 follows the line of the 73 ahead while the 29 attempts to hold the inside line. The angle of the 29 makes it unclear whether or not they would have made the corner, but the combination of the 29’s angle and the 27’s racing line cause the two cars to collide. The ensuing crash collects 4+ cars.

The 12 makes a lunge for the inside of the 85 at turn 1. The 12 does not achieve significant overlap until after turn-in, and then pushes wider earlier due to their entry angle. As the two cars pass the apex, the 12’s right front catches the 85’s left rear, sending them into the wall. This meatballs and damages them. As the 85 enters the next corner, the 117 attempts to swing around the outside. The 85 pushes wide just before the apex and hits the 117 in a mirror of the prior incident. The 117 also receives a meatball from hitting the outside wall.

The 12 makes a lunge for the inside of the 85 at turn 1. The 12 does not achieve significant overlap until after turn-in, and then pushes wider earlier due to their entry angle. As the two cars pass the apex, the 12’s right front catches the 85’s left rear, sending them into the wall. This meatballs and damages them. As the 85 enters the next corner, the 117 attempts to swing around the outside. The 85 pushes wide just before the apex and hits the 117 in a mirror of the prior incident. The 117 also receives a meatball from hitting the outside wall.

The 654 is behind the 767 on entry to turn 11. Under braking, the 654 brakes slightly late in reaction to the 767’s braking ahead. The 654 looks inside and makes contact with the 767’s right rear. This spins the 767 backwards into the wall, forcing them to pit under a meatball flag.

The 767’s braking point and entry speed on this lap was similar to prior laps where the 654 had been following, and similar to other cars of near pace.

Entering turn 6, the #02 is fully ahead of the #250, but leaves space to the inside. The #250 is not able to get into that space and achieve overlap. At the apex, they impact the right rear of the #02 and send them into a slide. The #02 loses two positions as a result.

At the apex of turn 6, the #661 is on the inside of the #18. The #661 accelerates early and pushes wide, impacting the left front and door of the #18. In the ensuing mayhem, the #18 makes minor contact with the #51 in a similar area. Ultimately, the #18’s front suspension is damaged and they are shown the meatball flag.

Exiting turn 8, the #119 is on the left side of the #29. The #119 swings right slightly more than the #29 in preparation for turn 9. The #119 contacts the #29’s left rear, destabilizing the #29. The #29 slides off-track and loses six positions. The stewards note there is minor netcode involved in this incident, but not enough to consider mitigating the penalty.

Under braking for turn 1, the #1 is behind the #490 and #73. As the leaders turn in for turn 1, the #1 goes deeper than the rest of the group and squeezes inside of the #490, who takes evasive action to avoid contact and turns away from the apex. The #1 then cuts across part of the grass before the apex, but fails to slow enough to prevent contact with the #73, the car ahead of the #490. The #1 misses the apex and taps the #73’s right rear, sending them into a slide that causes them to lose position to the #490. All cars continue unharmed.

At the apex of turn 13, the #57 leads the #02. The #57 gets a worse entry and exit, allowing the #02 to gain enough overspeed to pull alongside the #57 around the outside on the kerbing and within track limits. As the kerbing runs out, the #02 begins moving left to get fully back onto the asphalt. At this point, the #02 only barely has overlap, and the #57 leaves about exactly one car’s width between his car and the edge of the track for the #02 to fit into. The #02, most likely fearing contact, backs out of the space.
The 00 car makes contact with the rear of the 83 car, causing the 83 car to spin.
The 187 car makes contact with the rear of the 333 car, causing the 333 car to spin.

The 76 makes an over-under attempt on car 388 under braking for turn 8. Car 76 goes from the left of car 388 on the straight, to the right of car 388 on exit. Car 76 is well alongside car 388 into the narrow section before the fountain part of the track. The two cars make slight contact and 388 is spun into the wall.

Ahead of Car 6 in turn 2 there is a concertina effect happening with some light collisions. Car 6 takes avoiding action to the right, and lightly taps 119 who is looking to move around to the right. Car 119 is turned into the wall and takes damage, as well as other cars collected.

Car 26 has overlap with Car 57 through turn 6. Car 26 loses overlap between turns 6 and 7. Car 26 makes a move on car 57 into turn 7, however they did not have overlap before car 57 began turning in for turn 7. Car 26 makes contact with car 57, causing car 57 to stop and wait for the field to pass.

Car 3 gets a bad exit from turn 10 and car 999 capitalizes on this and achieves overlap alongside the right side of car 3. Car 3 begins to move to the right to squeeze car 999 and does not leave enough space at the apex of turn 11. Car 3 turns in without leaving adequate space for Car 999 making contact with Car 999 and spinning across their nose. Other cars behind also get collected in the resulting crash. Car 3 squeezed Car 999 and did not leave adequate space on the track to safely make the corner.

Car 38 is leading car 312 out of turn 10. Car 312 gets slight overlap on car 38 before turning into turn 11. The cars make contact and both cars are spun, and collect other cars with them. Both cars had adequate room to avoid contact, and the stewards feel both cars share responsibility for the incident.

After incident #3, Car 999 and others are leaving the pit lane while the leaders are coming around turn 1. In the drivers meeting the admins specifically offered guidance and instructions in this scenario for cars leaving the pit a lap down to let the cars on track by. It was also stated that the relative box gives misleading information when exiting pit late when cars are near turn 1. This guidance and instruction was not followed. Car 999 leaves the pits and car 13 comes around turn 1 into turn 2 making contact with Car 999. Many other cars are caught in the wreck. Car 661 and Car 41 also did not yield, but did not directly wreck another car so they received a warning. Car 27 also left the pits and rejoined the race a lap down; however, at an expected speed and with a more clear gap to the cars behind.

It was also stated that the relative box gives misleading information when exiting pit late when cars are near turn 1. This guidance and instruction was not followed. Car 661 and Car 41 also did not yield, but did not directly wreck another car so they received a warning. Car 27 also left the pits and rejoined the race a lap down; however, at an expected speed and with a more clear gap to the cars behind.

Similar to Incident 5, car 23 exits the pits in the middle of a group of cars on the lead lap. Car 23 fails to yield under blue flags for approximately a full lap. The warning comes from consistency with 661, and 41 penalties in incident #5. The guidance outlined in the drivers meeting was disregarded.
Car 02 makes contact with the rear of car 6 under braking for turn 13 (the final hairpin) and causes Car 6 to spin and lose time/positions.

Car 02 is looking to pass Car 25 at the apex of turn 1. Car 25 is looking to under-over the car ahead of them for turn 2-3 ahead. Car 25 is not aware of car 02 getting alongside, and car 02 is not aware of Car 25’s intention to make a move. The cars collide and carry on racing.
Car 77 makes contact with the right rear of car 29 in the middle of turn 13. Car 29 slides and loses positions as a result.
Car 13 brakes slightly late and makes contact with car 04 causing car 04 to lose positions as a result.
Car 119 brakes slightly late and makes contact with car 21. Car 21 receives a meatball as a result.
Car 187 makes contact with the rear of car 119 immediately after incident 2. Car 119 is spun around but can continue the race.
Car 51 brakes late into turn 11, and makes contact with car 11 who had already begun turning in for the corner. Car 11 is spun and loses substantial time as a result.
Car 3 makes a late lunge to try to pass car 38 into turn 14. Car 3 did not have overlap at the time of the move, and the contact causes car 38 to spin and come to a stop around a blind corner.
Car 57 runs deep into turn 17 (the final corner). Upon rejoining the track car 57 makes contact with the right rear of car 21, causing car 21 to hit the wall.

Car 661 misses their braking point for turn 1 and attempts to avoid contact with the 250 ahead by turning in for the corner late. In doing so, they make contact with the left rear of the 83 and cause them to spin.

The 57, 250, and 91 are three-wide left to right on corner entry. The 250 makes minor contact with the 02 ahead on corner entry. The 02’s slower entry speed allows the 57 to get inside of the 02 with significant overlap, making it three wide with the 312 on the outside. The 02 turns in, perhaps not fully aware the 57 is inside, and forces the 57 onto the curbs until realizing they need to give more space. The 02 opens the wheel for a moment right as the 312 cuts in a little further to attack the apex for corner exit. The right front of the 02 contacts the left rear of the 312, and they lose 4 positions from the ensuing slide. The 57 and 02 make minor side to side contact as the 02 avoids the sliding 312. The stewards determined the only penalizable incident here was the 312’s slide, and fault for it could not be assigned to any one driver.

At the exit of turn 5, the 02 does not leave enough room on the racing surface for car 41 on the outside of the track. The 02 then stays alongside the 41 and challenges them into the braking zone of turn 7, where the 41 pulls fully ahead of the 02 again.

In the braking zone for the entry of the 7,8,9 chicane, the 119 and 312 are side by side left to right. The 119 turns in, possibly a little early, while the 312 begins a later turn in. They make contact, which sends the 312 over the apex of turn 7, cutting it completely. The two cars remain alongside due to a small boost of throttle from the 312 as they come back on track next to the turn 8 apex. At the bottom of the chicane, the 312’s front left makes contact with the right rear of the 119, with a very minor amount of netcode. The 119 is kicked into a minor slide, allowing the 312 to get fully ahead and open a small gap.

Due to an incident ahead, the 3 spins to the right side of the track just before the apex of turn 4. The field ahead of the 02 partially slows as this happens. The 767 on the far left of the track is hemmed in by the 27 in front and then slows down further as they see the incident ahead unfold. When they turn in for turn 4, the 02 is still half a car length behind and the 25 is alongside them to the right. The 02 keeps the throttle engaged up until making contact with the right rear of the 767 with their front left while trying to fit between the 767 and 25 mid-corner. This destroys the 767’s suspension and they spin at turn 5, then tow. At contact, the speed differential between the two cars was 24kph.

After the chaos at turn 4, the field is bunched together entering turn 5. The 27 and 76 are side by side on the left side of the track to give space to the 187 and 25 ahead on the right side of the track. The 41 and 119 are similarly positioned, behind and to the right of the 27 and 76, directly behind the 187 and 25. Under braking, the 41 and 119 become four wide with the 27 and 76 on the inside. No single driver intentionally makes it four wide, but everyone judges the braking differently and this is the result. At turn in, the 119’s front left makes contact with the 76’s right rear. This straightens both cars out enough that the 41’s left rear then makes contact with the 119’s right front. The 41 slides and loses multiple positions.

Immediately after Incident #6, the 25 is in the far outside lane after losing out on the outside to the 27 and 187 mid-corner after contact with the 187. The 76 unwinds their steering for a moment mid-corner as the 25 turns in more, and the 76’s front right meets the 25’s left rear. The 25 enters a slide which sandwiches the 76 into the 02, and they all three slam together at the same time door to door to door. This severely damages the front suspension of the 76. The 76 and 25 lose out to multiple cars after the contact.

The two drivers remain side by side as they approach turn 7, where the 21 makes it three wide on the right side. The 25 moves slightly left in the braking zone as the 76 is pulled even more so to the right due to their suspension damage. The two make contact and the 25 is sent into the barriers on the left, causing terminal damage.
The 57 makes contact with the rear of the 89 at the turn in of turn 5. This causes the 89 to enter a slide and lose three positions as a result.

The 80 is behind the 04 and 18, who are side by side and on approach to turn 7. The 04 is on the left side of the track, with the 18 and 80 on the right. The 80 looks for a chance to follow the 18 through in the chicane but the 04 stays fully clear of them under braking. The 04 turns in to take the apex, but the 80 goes slightly deep and their left front makes contact with the 04’s right rear. This severely damages the suspension of the 04 and forces them to cut turn 8’s apex. The 04 spins a couple of turns later, possibly due to the damage, and eventually pits for repairs despite no meatball flag.

The 1 misses their braking and comes from at least three car lengths behind to make contact with the left rear of the 77. The 77 is spun sideways without any perceivable damage but has to come to a complete stop, losing 6 positions. They then tow, but this is most likely due to them receiving a black flag for hitting the incident limit.

The 661 exits turn 1 with the 654 behind. The 654 looks inside to try to get inside of the 661 under braking for turn 2 and there is potentially enough space to the right of the 661 to do so, but they misjudge their attack. The 654’s left front makes contact with the right rear of the 661 at a high speed mid-corner. The 661 is sent off the track with damage, losing two positions on track in the process.

The 12 and 18 enter turn 11 side by side, left to right. As the cars pass the apex, the 18’s line widens as the 12 turns-in, causing the 12 to make contact with the left door of the 18. The two cars glue together until reaching the outside wall, where the 18 is turned 90 degrees sideways facing the wall with the 12 stuck behind them against the wall. The 12 tows very quickly. 

The 18, possibly trying to get out of the 12’s way, reverses at least one car’s width backwards before stopping again. This causes the 04 to hit the left rear of the 18, causing damage and bringing the 04 to a dead stop. This causes the 27 and 6 behind to stack up, and leaves the 27 stuck behind the 18 as a result until the 18 also tows.

312 exits pit lane, under blue flags to the 58, 85, and 767 behind. The 58 is about half a second behind entering the fountain. On exit of turn 5, the 312 pulls to the left, appearing to prepare to let the group by. But the 312 holds their line and defends into turns 6/7. The 312 then allows the 58 to their inside for the run to turn 8, lifting and allowing the 85 to pass into the corner as well. The 312 then pulls to the right and lets the 767 safely through. 

On entry to turn 9, the 312 stays to the right to battle with the 57, who is on the same lap. The two cars make contact at the apex and the 57 slides into the wall, suffering rear-end damage.

The stewards note that with 3 cars directly behind, the section between turns 5 and 8 can be awkward to yield through, and for the most part this was handled well. However, taking a defensive line while under blue flags to prevent lead lap cars from passing is unpredictable and prohibited.

The 25 and 312 begin braking for turn 11 side by side, left to right. The 25 is far left and on the normal racing line, the 312 is 2-3 car widths to the right of the 25 on a narrow entry. At the apex, the 312’s line widens as the 25’s stays mostly consistent in terms of distance to the apex. The 25’s right front catches the 312’s left rear, and the two come to a stop to detach the cars. The 312 must drive fully backwards and circle around in the runoff area. The 25 reverses momentarily and then resumes from a full stop, still facing forward. 

The stewards recognize the difficulty of navigating this corner two-wide, but note the 312 was still very narrow on entry and wider than usual on exit in this incident.

There are two laps to go, and the leaders, 1 and 80, are within three tenths of each other. The 1 exits turn 8 about half a second behind the blue-flagged 83 and 72, who go side by side into turn 9, The 72 completes the overtake, the action causing both cars to lose almost all of the gap they had to the 1. Entering turn 11, the 1 attempts an overtake on the 83. The 1 does not have significant overlap, and the 83 does not appear to anticipate the move. The 1 contacts the right rear of the 83, sending it into a small slide. The two cars bounce off of each other one more time, clearing space for the 80 to overtake the 1 after the incident.

The stewards note that while the 83 and 72 were under blue flags, the 1 had only just cleared another blue flag car in the prior turn 8, and was half a second back. The section of the track they entered starting with turn 9 is not an area where it is easy or recommended to serve blue flags. The stewards agree that more patience was required from the lead cars in this situation.

It is the final lap. The 80 crosses over the pit exit line enough under braking for turn 1 that they collect the slowdown penalty. The 1 is less than three tenths behind. The 80 takes a slight lift into the fountain, but then brakes earlier and harder for turn 4 than expected, causing the 1 to make minor direct contact with their rear. The 80 had slowed to ~93kph before the contact occurred at the turn in point. On the previous lap, the 80’s speed was ~98kph minimum for the entire corner and ~100kph at the same point. 

The 80 reaches turn 8, having still not served the slowdown, and takes a defensive line after lifting on corner entry which forces the 1 to go side-by-side with them. The 80 goes slightly deep and pulls ahead, but has to slow to avoid hitting the barrier. This forces both cars to slow at the apex far more than normally required. At some point through turn 8, the 80 finally clears the slowdown. The stewards agree that these actions, especially the turn 4 incident, rise to the level of receiving a penalty.

The 20 and 187 are side-by-side exiting turn 5. The 187 moves back to the left to maximize the next corner, but moves slightly too far and makes contact with the right door of the 20, pushing them aside. The 187 completed the overtake and both continued undamaged.

The 18 is behind 187 through corners 1 and 2. The 18 takes a wide exit out of turn 2. In the transition between turns 2 and 3, this leaves the 18 far to the left. The 18 moves left to right to open up the corner, beginning to overlap the 187 at the same time. The 18 makes contact with the left rear of the 187 as they enter the braking zone and begin to turn in, causing the 187 to spin and fall to the back of the field. The 661 is forced off track by the 187’s sliding car.

It is the last lap. Beginning to brake for the final chicane, the 661 is over a car length ahead of the 21, but more than a lane further to the inside of the track as well. The 661 brakes slightly early, the 21 brakes later and turns in towards the apex while the 661 holds their place on track and delays turning in. The 21 makes contact with the rear of the 661, causing both to slide off track. The 661 is terminally damaged and cannot finish the race. The 21 limps to the finish.

Entering the braking zone for turn 1, the #654 is alongside the #76 on the inside. The #654 misses the braking point and cannot slow in time for the apex, aiming for a gap between the #661 and #83 ahead to minimize the contact. The #654 flies across the nose of the #661, slightly slowing them while sending the #654 spinning out into the runoff. All cars continue unharmed.

The #02 makes a slightly late lunge into turn 6, not having significant overlap before the turn-in point. Although the #02 reaches the #57’s door before the apex and properly slows for the corner, the #57 fails to see the #02 and react. The two cars make contact and the #57 is spun backwards.

The #72 carries too much speed through turn 10 compared to the #119 ahead, causing them to make contact with the #119’s right rear. This kicks them sideways and causes them to lose two positions. The #767 has to take avoiding action.

Through turn 1, the #85 is on the inside of the #58, who pulls fully ahead as they exit the corner. As the #85 moves to fill the space behind the #58 for slipstream, the #18 has attempted to slot in on the outside of the #85 where the #58 used to be as they come off the exit kerb. When the two cars make contact, the #18 has only had overlap for ~1 second. The #18 backs out and both continue unharmed. 

The stewards note that while you could accuse the #85 of blocking, they also had very little time to realize the #18 was in their blind spot after exiting the corner.

On lap 24, the #27 strikes a wall after turn 9 and damages their suspension. The #18 and #72 catch the #27 on the final lap. The #18 passes the #27 on the exit of turn 4. The #72 is not able to follow them, and becomes stuck behind the #27 throughout the next several corners. At turn 15, the #27 strikes the inside wall and the #72 is able to overtake them, but at this point has lost ~1 second to the #18 and cannot challenge them before the race ends. The #27 finishes the race without receiving a black flag, as they only carried the meatball flag for 3 full laps. 

The stewards note that while the #27’s car was damaged and well off the pace, they are within their right to defend their position with cars on the same lap as long as they are able to do so safely. The two drivers were also passing through a section of track where it is difficult to intentionally allow another driver to pass. The stewards determined the #27 did not take any action that endangered the #18 or #72.
